newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan December export orders below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan December export orders below expectations.

text.p: The 0.96 percent annual rise in December foreign orders for Taiwan goods, confirmed on Tuesday by the economics ministry, was below the average forecast in a January 16 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.

The December rise contributed to a 1996 full-year orders rise of 4.76 percent compared to 1995, the economics ministry said in releasing its official monthly report. Ministry officials first disclosed the indicators on Monday.
Table of export data in millions of U.S. dollars:
The December orders figure came in lower than the average 1.64 percent projection that resulted from a January 16 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.

Orders for the island's star industry -- electronics -- edged up 0.2 percent to US$1.516 billion in December from a year earlier and gained 4.7 percent from November. Orders from the United States accounted for 29.35 percent.
December orders for information and telecommunications products decreased 9.24 percent to US$1.502 billion, of which the United States accounted for 34.37 percent.
Orders for textile products rose 1.17 percent to US$1.293 billion, with Hong Hong accounting for 35.45 percent.
Orders from the United States totalled US$2.792 billion in December, down an annual 3.72 percent, followed by Hong Kong orders at US$1.992 billion, which were up 0.45 percent.
Japanese orders fell 8.04 percent to US$1.213 billion while European orders jumped 20.28 percent to US$1.72 billion.

In the whole of 1996, export orders totalled US$118.959 billion, with orders for electronic products rising 4.25 percent to US$17.002 billion and those for information and telecom products jumping 19.03 percent to US$18.15 billion.
U.S. orders totalled US$34.962 billion in 1996 while those from Hong Kong slid 1.49 percent to US$22.010 billion.
Japanese orders gained 8.47 percent to US$15.875 billion while European orders rose 14.89 percent to US$18.366 billion.
